blocks.prompt: 9 Suppose the population of a coastal city follows a sinusoidal pattern due to seasonal migration. The population of the city over the course of a year can be modeled by the equation: \(P(t) = 70000 + 10000\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{6}t - \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\), \(P(t)\) is the population at time \(t\) (\(t\) is the time in months, with \(t = 0\) corresponding to January 1st). where \(t\) denoted the months in a year. (a) Find the population of a city at \(t = 7\) months
steps:
Work out the angle
\[\tfrac{7\pi}{6} - \tfrac{\pi}{2} = \tfrac{7\pi}{6} - \tfrac{3\pi}{6}\]
\[= \tfrac{4\pi}{6} = \tfrac{2\pi}{3} = 120^{\circ}\]
Why: Common denominator 6.

Check
\[60000 \le 65000 \le 80000 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Within 10000 of the average 70000.

blocks.prompt: 9 Suppose the population of a coastal city follows a sinusoidal pattern due to seasonal migration. The population of the city over the course of a year can be modeled by the equation: \(P(t) = 70000 + 10000\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{6}t - \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\), \(P(t)\) is the population at time \(t\) (\(t\) is the time in months, with \(t = 0\) corresponding to January 1st). where \(t\) denoted the months in a year. (b) Find the maximum population
blocks.explanation:
Largest value of \(a + b\cos(\ldots)\).
Plan: cosine at most 1.
steps:
Given: \(P(t) = 70000 + 10000\cos(\frac{\pi}{6}t - \frac{\pi}{2})\).
To find: the maximum of \(P\).
Method: \(\cos \le 1\), so \(P \le 70000 + 10000\).

Use the range of cosine
\[-1 \le \cos(\ldots) \le 1\]
\[60000 \le P(t) \le 80000\]
Why: Multiply by 10000 and add 70000.

When it happens
\[\tfrac{\pi}{6}t - \tfrac{\pi}{2} = 0 \Rightarrow t = 3\]
Why: Cosine is 1 at angle 0; \(t = 3\) months is 1st April.

Check
\[P(3) = 70000 + 10000\cos 0 = 80000 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The maximum is actually reached.
